paper_metadata.title: Effect of Al addition on oxidation behavior of Nb-based refractory alloys

evidence.quote: the effect of Al addition on the oxidation behavior of some newly developed Nb-based refractory alloys, Nb79.5−xHf15W5.5Alx (x= 4, 8, 12, at. %), was investigated and benchmarked using the commercial WC3009 alloy.
we modified a commercial Nb-based refractory alloy, WC3009 (Nb-30Hf-9W, wt. %, or Nb75.2Hf19.2W5.6, at. %) and developed a Nb 79.5−xHf15W5.5Alx (x = 4, 8, 12, all in at. %) alloy system.
WC3009 was selected as the benchmark alloy due to its good tensile ductility at room temperature and its ability to retain high strength up to 1200°C

attributes.composition: Nb and W enriched in dendritic region; Hf and Al in inter-dendritic region

evidence.quote: A typical EDS elemental mapping from the 8Al alloy, presented in Fig. 2, shows dendritic and inter-dendritic features, with the segregation of Nb and W with high melting points in the dendritic region, while Hf and Al with relatively low melting points in the inter-dendritic region.
The average grain size of the WC3009 alloy is 30.64 μm.
the average grain size of the 4Al sample is the largest, reaching 44.52 μm
the average grain size of the 12Al sample is the smallest, reaching 36.87μm
WC3009 has the lowest hardness of 278 (HV5)
a reduction in grain size contributes to an increase in the material’s yield stress (in addition to the solid solution strengthening effect due to Al)
The increase in Al content leads to grain refinement, which may be because the increasing Al content limits the growth kinetics of the grains and thus forms a finer grain structure.

With linear oxidation kinetics, the oxidation process is controlled by the interface reaction, and the oxygen reacts directly with the sample surface to form an oxide layer, but this layer is thin and does not significantly hinder further oxidation.

This is due to the gradual thickening of the oxide layer, which hinders the penetration of oxygen and other diffusers (e.g., nitrogen), and the oxidation process begins to be dominated by diffusion control.
